tasks.title: One per-patient scheduler for every N (new module pool.py)
tasks.test_approach: Unit tests with module-level picklable worker functions in tests/pool_workers.py, parametrized over N=1 and N=2: result order, bounded submission (worker records start/end into files under tmp_path), hold-by-key, abort on an internal-error result and on an exception escaping the worker, Ctrl-C (KeyboardInterrupt raised in the N=1 path and from the parent wait), each consumer run under a thread join timeout to catch hangs. Worker logging checked with capfd in an N=2 run.
criteria: N=1 calls the worker function directly in the calling process (no executor); N>1 runs the same worker function on ProcessPoolExecutor(N); both go through the same scheduling code, with no separate legacy loop

The executor is built with mp_context=multiprocessing.get_context('spawn') on every Python version (the venv is 3.13, whose Linux default is fork; forkserver workers keep the fd 2 of the test that started the server, so capfd misses their output in later tests, checked 2026-11-05); a test asserts an N=2 worker does not see a monkeypatch made in the parent
At most N tasks are submitted to the executor at any time; the next is submitted only when one completes
Results are handed to the caller in input (sorted) order regardless of completion order
A task carrying a hold key is not started while another task with the same key is running; it starts after that one completes

When the caller signals abort, or an exception escapes a worker, nothing further is submitted, running tasks finish and their results are delivered, then the scheduler returns; it never calls shutdown(cancel_futures=True) inside a wait loop (vault: processpool-cancel-futures-hangs-as-completed)

An exception escaping a worker (including BrokenProcessPool) is reported to the caller as an internal failure carrying only the exception type name; its message, traceback and _RemoteTraceback are never formatted, logged or chained
On KeyboardInterrupt nothing further is submitted and the interrupt propagates after running tasks end; tests prove no hang (join timeout)

The pool initializer configures logging with format '%(message)s' at the parent's root logger level (passed via initargs), so a worker log.info line reaches stderr in an N=2 run (vault: spawned-worker-without-logging-config-only-warning-survives)
After KeyboardInterrupt, a task that later returns a result keeps its row; a task that ends with KeyboardInterrupt or any exception adds no row; neither exception is ever formatted
A held task does not block later unrelated tasks: they may be submitted ahead of it; results are still delivered in input order
tests/pool_workers.py holds every module-level test worker function the later tasks need, including convert, preprocess, organize-read and organize-copy raisers selected by patient folder name
Full suite and ruff pass

tasks.title: convert and preprocess on the scheduler
tasks.test_approach: Existing suite (N=1 through the scheduler) must pass unchanged in behaviour. New tests on synthetic trees of at least 3 patients compare N=1 vs N=2 output file names, data-file bytes and report rows. Abort tests use the internal worker-callable argument with a module-level test function from tests/pool_workers.py that raises for one chosen patient.
criteria: convert(..., workers=N) and preprocess(..., workers=N) run one patient per task; preprocess gains a workers keyword defaulting to 1
For a synthetic tree of at least 3 patients, N=2 writes the same file names and byte-identical data files and the same report rows in the same order as N=1

The parent claims the casefolded input folder name: under --overwrite a repeat gets REASON_NAME_CLAIMED without being dispatched (first in sorted order wins, as today); without --overwrite a repeat is held until the first completes and then runs as today, and N=2 rows equal N=1 rows
OSError in a patient gives that patient's REASON_IO_ERROR row inside the worker, as today

Another exception in a patient: the worker computes crash_site and logs the existing type/module/line line; the parent adds the REASON_INTERNAL row, starts no further patient, keeps the rows of patients already running, writes the report and raises ConvertAborted / PreprocessAborted; with N=2 the call returns (timeout-guarded test) and capfd stderr holds no exception message text

convert logs 'convert: %.1f s total, %.1f s reading (summed over patients), %.1f s converting (summed over patients), %d files, workers %d', where total is wall clock and converting is each patient's own time minus its reading, summed; outcome and replaced/kept counts are unchanged for N=1; the TIMING regexes in tests are updated to match
examples/synthetic_workflow.py keeps its __main__ guard and runs with workers=2 for all three stages
convert and preprocess docstrings describe workers as patient processes

The internal seam keyword `_patient_fn` (organize: `_read_fn` for task A, `_copy_fn` for task B) replaces only the inner per-patient call; the in-worker OSError and Exception conversion (and crash_site logging) still wraps it

Existing tests that monkeypatch or use caplog run at workers=1 only and their N>1 parametrization is dropped; the 1-vs-4 equality tests (test_organize.py:549, test_convert.py:682 and :1324) keep N=4 because they patch nothing
Full suite and ruff pass

tasks.title: organize on the scheduler: read task, parent claims, copy task
tasks.test_approach: Existing organize suite passes (N=1). New N=1 vs N=2 equality test on a synthetic export of at least 3 patients including two folders with one PatientID and one refused (no SOP UID) folder under --overwrite with an existing output. Abort test through the worker-callable argument. A resume test (no --overwrite, outputs present) asserts nothing is copied (no .partial created) for skipped patients.
criteria: Task A (worker) walks, reads and groups one source folder and returns the sanitized name, a raw refusal or the per-plan and misc path lists (paths only), the unreadable count, the walked file count and reading seconds; headers are read once per run

The parent, in sorted source order, computes the kept status of a refused patient exactly as organize.py does today and does not claim its name; then claim check (REASON_NAME_CLAIMED), recover, existence check (OUTCOME_SKIPPED / REASON_EXISTS), then submits task B
Task B (worker) copies into .<name>.partial and publishes as today; nothing is copied for a patient that is refused or skipped
For the synthetic export, N=2 gives the same output tree, the same report rows in order and the same replaced/kept counts as N=1
An unexpected exception in organize: REASON_INTERNAL row, crash-site log line from the worker, no further patient started, report written, OrganizeAborted raised; no exception message text on stderr

The internal seam keyword `_patient_fn` (organize: `_read_fn` for task A, `_copy_fn` for task B) replaces only the inner per-patient call; the in-worker OSError and Exception conversion (and crash_site logging) still wraps it

Existing tests that monkeypatch or use caplog run at workers=1 only and their N>1 parametrization is dropped; the 1-vs-4 equality tests (test_organize.py:549, test_convert.py:682 and :1324) keep N=4 because they patch nothing

organize.REASON_INTERNAL = 'an unexpected error stopped the organizing; the report lists what was finished'; its row is PatientRow(sanitize_path_component(folder.name), 0, 0, 0, OUTCOME_REFUSED, REASON_INTERNAL)

An OSError in task A, task B or the parent's recover gives that patient's REASON_IO_ERROR row and warning, and the run goes on; ValueError(REASON_OUTSIDE_ROOT) propagates as today and is not turned into REASON_INTERNAL
organize's timing line labels reading and copying seconds '(summed over patients)', total stays wall clock; the TIMING regex in test_organize.py is updated
Full suite and ruff pass
